clue.text: Bird in current left to the end

indicators.note: says the letter for left is shifted along to sit at the very end of the word for current

parts.note: a current is a flow of water or air

explanation.surface: A bird floats in a current while something is pushed to the end of the stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the end' moves the L of FLOW to the back, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fowl is a bird, especially a domestic one such as a chicken or duck.

clue.text: Pet: I will occupy identical place around front of couch

indicators.note: the letter I is said to occupy, or sit inside, the word for identical

parts.note: identical things are the same

indicators.note: the word for place is wrapped around the opening letter of couch

parts.note: a seat is a place, as in taking one's place

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, here taken from couch

explanation.surface: A pet owner announces they will claim the same spot around the couch as the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a verb but is the definition: a cat breed. 'will occupy' and 'around' each signal one piece going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siamese cat is a popular breed of domestic cat kept as a pet.

clue.text: Furniture item as yet unfinished

indicators.note: a word left unfinished loses its final letter, here the R of the phrase for as yet

parts.note: so far means as yet, up to now

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture that has not been completed yet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people, a standard piece of furniture.

clue.text: Water filling everything in ranch? It's nothing to worry about

indicators.note: the built-up group of letters goes inside the word for ranch

parts.note: a ranch is a farm, typically for cattle

indicators.note: the word for water fills the word for everything, sitting inside it

parts.note: all means everything
the sea is a body of water

explanation.surface: Flooding has reached every part of the ranch, yet someone insists it is no cause for concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' and 'in' are two nested insertions: the inner result goes inside the word for ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: A false alarm is a warning that proves groundless, so nothing that needed worrying over.

clue.text: Reward solver in a stroke

indicators.note: the word for the solver sits inside the word for a stroke

parts.note: a pat is a light stroke with the hand
the solver is addressed as you by the setter

explanation.surface: The solver is rewarded with a gentle pat, or a reward comes at a single stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay-out is a sum of money paid, such as a prize or compensation, so a reward.

clue.text: Problem in perceiving my work is awful at the outset

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work, especially of music

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their work looks awful from the start because they cannot see well.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia, short-sightedness, is a defect of vision, so a problem with seeing distant things.

clue.text: Millions enthralled by me and my historic site

indicators.note: the letter for millions is held captive between the words for me and my

parts.note: taken as written
the setter is Phi, so the setter's own, my, is PHI'S

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that millions are captivated by them and their famous site.
explanation.walkthrough: This puzzle's setter signs as Phi, so 'my' means the setter's own; 'enthralled by' puts the letter for millions between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Memphis was the capital of ancient Egypt, whose ruins are a famous historic site.

clue.text: Very revolutionary beat associated with a piece of music

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word for beat is read backwards

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: A very radical beat is linked with a musical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reads as radical but signals reading the word for beat backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a composition for one or two instruments, usually in several movements.

clue.text: Patriotic song at each show's going wild

indicators.note: letters that go wild run riot and end up in a new order

explanation.surface: At every performance the crowd goes wild for a patriotic number.
explanation.walkthrough: Scots Wha Hae is a Robert Burns song, long treated as an unofficial Scottish national anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: This Burns song rallies Scots behind Robert the Bruce at Bannockburn, so it is a patriotic anthem.

clue.text: Recalled idea from internet when fixing British Library logo

indicators.note: the abbreviation is fixed firmly inside the turned-round word
called back, so the word for an internet idea is read in reverse

parts.note: a meme is an idea or image spread online
BL is the abbreviation for the British Library

explanation.surface: A viral idea is recalled while the British Library's logo is being repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reverses MEME to EMEM; BL is fixed in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a symbol or badge representing an organisation, much like a logo.

clue.text: Where one might discuss food, including nightcaps?

indicators.note: the word for food takes in the word for nightcaps

parts.note: chow is slang for food
nightcaps are hats worn in bed, so hats in general

explanation.surface: A question about where people might talk over food and late-night drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nightcaps' looks like bedtime drinks, but it means headgear, HATS.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat show is a broadcast programme in which guests and a host talk things over.

clue.text: Cabin trunk, perhaps, taken round ship by English men?

definitions.note: a plural noun for the singular answer: the set consists of the chessmen

indicators.note: the word for the trunk is wrapped round the letters for ship and English

parts.note: a cabin trunk is an example of a chest
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A traveller's trunk is carried around a ship by Englishmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' looks like people carrying the trunk, but chessmen are the pieces, and a set of them is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chessmen are the pieces of a chess game, and together they make up the boxed set.

clue.text: Range of notes on fashion line implying something not the right size

parts.note: a scale is a run of musical notes in order
mode means fashion, as in a la mode

explanation.surface: A musical range paired with a fashion line hints that something is the wrong size.
explanation.definitionFit: A scale model is a replica built smaller or larger than the real thing, so deliberately off-size.

clue.text: Enthusiastic cry drawing attention about skill

indicators.note: the cry is placed about, around, the word for skill

parts.note: hey is a shout used to get someone's attention
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: An eager shout attracts notice about someone's talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty welcome is warm and vigorous, so hearty means enthusiastic.

clue.text: Marine creature runs, sheltering in trim beach after storm

indicators.note: the letter for runs takes shelter inside the rearranged letters
a storm leaves things tossed about, so the letters of trim beach are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sea creature scuttles off to shelter on a tidied beach after a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after storm' jumbles the letters to HEMITCRAB, and 'sheltering in' puts R third.
explanation.definitionFit: The hermit crab lives in the sea and borrows empty shells of other molluscs for protection.

clue.text: Crew has torn up outrageous legal document

indicators.note: torn into pieces, the letters of crew has are rearranged

parts.note: arrant means utter or outrageous, as in arrant nonsense

explanation.surface: A crew has ripped up a scandalous legal paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A search warrant is a court order authorising police to search premises, a legal instrument.

clue.text: Touching performance in a hat

indicators.note: the word for performance goes inside the slang word for a hat

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A moving show is put on by someone wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' looks like emotionally moving but means relating to touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to the sense of touch, so touching in the physical sense.

clue.text: Contracted disease from meat when hosted by soldier? Not here

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the disease is held inside the word for soldier, as a host holds a guest

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant
BSE, mad cow disease, abbreviated or contracted, was linked to eating infected beef

explanation.surface: A soldier caught a disease from eating meat and is off sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' looks like caught but means shortened: BSE is the abbreviation for bovine spongiform encephalopathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means away or not present, so not here.

clue.text: Drunken bum getting cut, swallowing litre

indicators.note: the shortened word swallows the letter for litre
the word for bum is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: bum is British slang for the bottom

explanation.surface: A drunken layabout gets hurt while gulping down a litre of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTOM cut to BOTTO takes in L.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely drunk.

clue.text: Greek character prodding a breeding dog? That's uncalled-for

indicators.note: the Greek letter pokes into the words that follow, sitting inside them

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog, used for breeding
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek is poking a breeding dog, and an onlooker says it is unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prodding' means the Greek letter is pushed into the middle of the dog, after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is a bit much means it goes too far, so it is excessive or unwarranted.

clue.text: Article covered in blood brought on board by ship-builder mostly something to be avoided

indicators.note: the letters are taken aboard, inside, the shortened name of the ship-builder
most of the name, dropping its last letter

parts.note: Noah built the ark in the Bible

indicators.note: the article is covered by, inside, the word for blood

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A bloodstained item taken aboard by a shipbuilder is something best kept clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the ark-builder's name; 'covered in' and 'brought on board by' are two nested insertions.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go area is a place people avoid or are barred from, so it should be shunned.

clue.text: Very worried after a force skips attack

indicators.note: the letters for a and force are skipped, left out of the word for very worried

parts.note: afraid means frightened, very worried
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious after a military unit misses an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault on a place, so an attack.

clue.text: Give way about a source of ore

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
a vein is a seam of ore in rock

explanation.surface: Something collapses around a seam being mined for ore.
explanation.definitionFit: To cave in is to collapse, or to yield under pressure, so to give way.

clue.text: Nothing set up about European ban

indicators.note: the reversed letters go about, around, the letter for European
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: Nothing has been arranged regarding a European prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OTV into VTO, which goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is the power to block or forbid a decision, so a ban.

clue.text: French are blocking the current proposition

indicators.note: the French word sits in the way, inside the word for the current one

parts.note: this means the present or current one, as in this week
es is French for are, as in tu es

explanation.surface: The French stand in the way of the present proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a statement or argument put forward to be defended, a proposition.

clue.text: British former Prime Minister missing last engagement

indicators.note: the statesman's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Clement Attlee was UK Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: A British ex-premier skips the final appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' looks like a date or betrothal but means a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is a military encounter between forces, so a battle.
